modeled using a suitable semi-empirical correlation. As for the skin friction coefficient, to evaluate the heat flux qw from the lateral wall, the semi-empirical relations

where the first term Nu <sup>0</sup> expresses the Nusselt number for the case of constant properties flow (which grossly represents the adiabatic flow) in rough tubes; the second, Ch, is
the correction that applies in the case of fluid with variable temperature. For the problem of interest, the Nusselt number of the constant properties flow depends on the
bulk Reynolds number Re based on the hydraulic diameter of the channel crosssection, the bulk Prandtl number Pr and, in the case of rough tubes, the wall relative
roughness e: Nu <sup>0</sup> ¼ Nu <sup>0</sup> (Re, Pr, e). The correction factor Ch, because it takes into
account the effect of the nonadiabatic case, mainly depends on the ratio between
the wall and fluid temperature: Tw=T. To fit the semi-empirical correlations to the
quasi-2-D model, the Nusselt number is evaluated at the local abscissa y. In fact,
as the wall temperature and the fluid properties vary with the radial abscissa y, the
Nusselt number (and thus the heat transfer coefficient on the lateral wall) vary with y.

2.4. Equations of State

In the selected flow model, the density and the temperature have been selected
as independent thermodynamic variables, and it has been implicitly assumed that the
other thermodynamic variables (pressure and enthalpy) can be obtained by suitable
equations of state (EOS), which are written in the following general form:

p ¼ pðq; TÞ and H ¼ Hðq; TÞ ð19Þ

and that the fluid molecular properties (viscosity and thermal conductivity),
can be evaluated by proper thermodynamic relations which can be written in the following general form:

m ¼ mðq; TÞ and k ¼ kðq; TÞ ð20Þ

Note, that the proposed flow model does not refer to any particular EOS, and
thus the channel flow of any fluid can be described. This goal is achieved by considering general equations of state in the form of Eqs. (19) and (20), and governing
equations without any thermodynamic characterization of the working fluid.

2.5. Equation for the Velocity Profile

Aswillbeshownin thefollowingsections, themainfeaturesofthewall heat transfer
distribution in a channel section are: a peak value in the low-density, high-velocity region
and the strong heat transfer reduction in the proximity of channel section corners. These
features can be reproduced if the velocity distribution tends to zero close to the wall, and
presents a peak value that is located in the lower density region of the channel section. In
regards to the velocity peak value, it is due to the temperature asymmetric distribution in
the channel cross-section. Moreover, the greater the temperature difference the greater
the velocity peak value. Thus, it is possible to say that the velocity variation relative to
its mean value is equal to the temperature variation relative to its mean value; that is,
